is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates field populations of Anopheles funestus s.s. and Anopheles gambiae s.s. from Sud-Kivu, DRC (page 1340-1341).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for kdr (Vgsc L995F using Martinez-Torres et al. 1998 protocol) and ace-1R (Ace-1 G280S using Weill et al. 2003/2004 protocol) (page 1341).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 1341-1342 reports: 'The distribution of kdr and ace-1R mutations was investigated on 101 A. gambiae s.s. individuals. The frequency of the resistant kdr allele was almost fixed (98%, n=99) in A. gambiae s.s. populations. However, the ace-1R mutation was not detected in the Tchonka area.'

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquito larvae of Anopheles funestus and Anopheles gambiae were collected from natural breeding sites in Tchonka, Sud-Kivu, DRC and reared to adults for bioassays and PCR (page 1341).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article presenting original field bioassay and molecular surveillance data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Tchonka village (GPS coordinates: 2°19'20.29"S, 27°32'25.90"E), Lulingu health district, Shabunda territory, Sud-Kivu province, DRC (page 1340).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from April to November 2018 (page 1341).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary field collections conducted by MSF and research partners between April and November 2018 in Tchonka.

supplement.evidence: Target marker frequency and sample size are reported directly in the main text (pages 1341-1342).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide susceptibility and resistance markers (Vgsc L1014F and Ace-1 G119S) in Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles funestus s.s. from Tchonka, Sud-Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2018. Bioassays revealed resistance to pyrethroids, DDT, and bendiocarb, but susceptibility to organophosphates and propoxur. The Vgsc L995F mutation frequency was 98% (n=99) in An. gambiae s.s., while Ace-1 G280S was not detected (0%, n=101).
